topic: Neural Network Learning and Intuitive Backpropagation
target_audience: University students or beginners in Artificial Intelligence

sections.title: The Learning Goal: Pixel the Robot's Task
lecture_lines: Meet Pixel, a robot learning to see.
Pixel's guesses are compared to the truth.
The error, or loss, shows how wrong he is.
animations: A blurry dog image appears on the left (#FFFFFF). Pixel (#00FF00) appears on the right with a thought bubble showing a toaster (#C0C0C0).
Text 'Toaster' (#FF0000) appears above Pixel. Text 'Dog' (#00FF00) appears above the image.
A bar graph labeled 'Loss' (#FFD700) rises to 80% height. Pixel looks sad (#FF0000).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Decision
lecture_lines: Networks use weights as adjustable control knobs.
High weights mean an input is very important.
A bias sets the baseline for every decision.
animations: Circles representing 'Floppy Ears' and 'Metal Texture' (#FFFFFF) flow arrows toward a central neuron (#00FFFF).
Knobs (#A9A9A9) appear on the arrows. The 'Floppy Ears' knob turns to a high setting (#FFFF00).
A 'Bias' slider (#FFA500) moves, and the neuron's output bulb (#FFFFFF) glows brighter.

sections.title: The Loss Landscape: Walking in the Fog
lecture_lines: Imagine the total error as a hilly landscape.
The height at any point is the loss.
Learning is finding the lowest valley.
We feel the slope to find the way down.
This slope is called the gradient.
animations: A 2D wavy line representing the loss landscape (#FFFFFF) appears through semi-transparent fog (#808080).
A vertical arrow labeled 'Loss Height' (#FF0000) follows the curve's peaks and valleys.
Pixel (#00FF00) stands on a steep part of the curve. He tilts to match the incline.
A bright arrow (#FFFF00) appears at Pixel's feet, pointing directly up the slope.
A star (#00FF00) marks the lowest point of the curve. The fog clears slightly.

sections.title: Backpropagation: Tracing the Blame
lecture_lines: To improve, we send error signals backward.
We ask which knobs caused the final mistake.
The chain rule connects every layer's influence.
Each connection gets a share of the blame.
This blame guides the direction of change.
animations: A red glow (#FF0000) starts at the output lightbulb and pulses back toward the neuron.
The connection for 'Metal Texture' flashes red (#FF0000) to indicate high blame.
Interlocked gears (#D3D3D3) rotate. One gear's movement affects the next in sequence.
Backward arrows (#FF4500) carry 'correction' values to each knob.
Numbers like -0.5 and +0.2 (#FFFFFF) appear next to the connection lines.

sections.title: The Adjustment: Nudging the Knobs
lecture_lines: We nudge the knobs based on the blame.
Each weight is adjusted by a small step.
The learning rate controls how far we move.
Small steps prevent overshooting the bottom.
Moving down the slope reduces the total error.
animations: Small vector arrows (#FFFF00) appear on the surface of each knob.
A slider labeled 'Learning Rate' (#00FF00) moves to a low value. The arrows shrink.
The 'Floppy Ear' knob rotates clockwise (#00FF00). The 'Metal' knob rotates counter-clockwise (#FF0000).
On the landscape, Pixel (#00FF00) slides a small distance toward the valley.
The movement stops precisely before the slope starts rising again.

sections.title: The Training Loop: Practice Makes Perfect
lecture_lines: Pixel repeats this process thousands of times.
With every example, the knobs become more precise.
Soon, Pixel identifies objects with high accuracy.
animations: A circular arrow (#FFFFFF) connects Forward, Loss, Backprop, and Update labels.

Images of dogs [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dog.svg] and toasters [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/toaster.svg] (#FFFFFF) flash rapidly in front of Pixel.
